correctness.rationale: Represent the kernel by (√a,cos x,sin x); diagonalize the two-site Gram matrix by symmetric/antisymmetric vectors. Integrated second moments are 2a²+u and 1−u, giving V=a+1−(2a²+u)/(t+2a+2u)−(1−u)/(t+2−2u), u=cos²(Δ/2). The derivative is −C/(t+2a+2u)²+t/(t+2−2u)², C=t+2a−4a²; its square-root sign witness is strictly increasing, positive at u=1, and has at most one zero. Endpoint sign at 0 yields the exact a_c(t) positive quadratic root. At a=1/2 the optimizer u=1/4; Taylor expansion at t=0 for a<1/2 gives 1−u ∼(a+1)√t/√(2a(1−2a)) and hence the quarter power. The rank-one Moore–Penrose result at exact collision exceeds the distinct-site limit by 1/2. Independent direct unsimplified 2×2 inverse and trigonometric moment checks were run at 30 positive parameter values; they corroborate, not replace, continuous global derivative proof.

value.rationale: For a rank-three periodic kernel, exactly two independently noisy landmarks form the first underdetermined nontrivial spatial design. A parameter-uniform 120° optimum and singular quarter-power collapse sharply distinguish low-noise duplicate observations from noiseless rank loss; a natural exact design and boundary result.

final_claim: For a>0 and independent-noise/ridge t>0, exact two-site IVAR minimization for k_a(x,y)=a+cos(x−y) has a unique antipodal/interior phase boundary a_c(t); a=1/2 has noise-independent optimal separation 2π/3 and each fixed 0<a<1/2 has a sharp t^(1/4) near-collision law; at exactly t=0 the pseudoinverse collision jumps by 1/2.
